notes: Salotto (living room) of the Milan apartment, the 'Display wall' (salotto-E in layout.json / layout.md), matching the room's blurb: 'glass display cases with open antique illustrated books, seashells and rare comics' plus 'a wooden cabinet with objects and hi-fi'. This full-resolution portrait (3225x2398) shows Eco leaning toward the camera in front of two of the three steel-and-glass vetrine cases (bookcase id salotto-vetrine) and the left edge of the dark wood cabinet (bookcase salotto-E / low art-book unit is out of frame to the left). Unlike shelved libraries elsewhere in the apartment, every book visible here is lying open flat on a glass shelf, displayed page-out rather than spine-out, showing woodcut/engraved illustrations and print blocks of antiquarian volumes (consistent with the Zanni banner crop of the same vitrines, already logged as zanni_banner_orig.jpg, 'open books, not spines'). No spine, title, or author text is legible on any book in the vitrines even after 2x LANCZOS upscaling and unsharp-mask sharpening of 20 overlapping 900px tiles plus several targeted high-zoom crops - the pages show only black-letter illustration blocks and body text too fine and blurred by camera shake/focus to resolve. The wood cabinet's top shelf (row 4) holds a single closed volume with an illustrated (comic/childrens-style, blue ground with a yellow figure) cover and what may be a two-volume boxed set with a red/cream spine, but again no legible lettering at this resolution. Below that shelf the same cabinet holds a hi-fi rack, CD spines, audio cassettes and a VHS tape (media, not books) and is not itemised as book rows. A stack of magazines/papers is visible edge-on at the bottom-left corner of the frame but is too foreshortened and blurred to read any titles. Overall this photo, despite being the highest-resolution free image of Eco in this room, yields no legible book spines; it is included for completeness and room/wall identification only.
